note.explanation: Mean, median, and mode describe the centre or most common value in a data set. Find the mean by adding all the values and dividing by how many there are. Find the median after arranging the values in order. Find the mode by checking which value occurs most often.
examples: For 2, 4, 6, the median is 4, and there is no mode because no value repeats.
note.checkAnswer: The values in order are 2, 4, 8, 10. The two middle values are 4 and 8, so the median is (4 + 8)/2 = 6.
note.simple: Mean is the sharing-out average, median is the middle after sorting, and mode is the value that occurs most often.
note.title: Mean, Median, and Mode
steps: For the mean, add all the data values and divide by the number of values.
For the median, arrange the values in ascending order.
If there are an odd number of values, take the middle value; if there are an even number, average the two middle values.
For the mode, count how often each value appears and choose the value or values with the highest frequency.
note.answer: Mean = sum of all data points divided by number of data points; median = the middle value after ordering; mode = the most frequent value.

explain.title: Mean
explain.body: The mean, also known as the average, is the sum of all the values in a data set divided by the number of values. It represents the central value of a data set.

explain.title: Median
explain.body: The median is the middle value of a data set when the values are arranged in ascending or descending order. If the number of values is odd, the median is the middle value. If the number of values is even, the median is the average of the two middle values.

explain.title: Finding the median
explain.body: Arrange the data in ascending order first. For an odd number of values, use position (n + 1)/2. For an even number of values, average the values at positions n/2 and n/2 + 1.

explain.title: Mode
explain.body: The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A data set may have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode at all.

explain.title: Finding the mode
explain.body: Count the frequency of each value in the data set. The value with the highest frequency is the mode. If two or more values share the highest frequency, they are all modes; if every value occurs equally often, there is no mode.

mistakes: Finding the median before arranging the values in order.
Choosing just one of the two middle values when the number of values is even; take their average instead.
Dividing the sum by the wrong number of values when calculating the mean.
Assuming a data set always has a mode; it can have more than one mode or no mode.
Giving a mode without checking which value has the highest frequency.
